Marvel Rivals is a fun and chaotic hero shooter that really captures the spirit of Marvel. The characters feel unique, and the team-up mechanics add a fresh layer of strategy that keeps matches exciting. Visually, it’s vibrant and polished, with well-designed maps that encourage dynamic gameplay.

It’s not perfect—balance can be inconsistent, and teamwork plays a big position in how enjoyable matches feel—but overall, it’s a strong and entertaining entry in the genre with plenty of potential.

Every new hero lately is just broken. They say they're balancing for fun not necessarily for fairness, which is a horrible take for a competitive hero shooter. Many of your audience have different mains and want their mains to shine in certain comps and have good enough counterplay in the meta. By not catering to most of your mains, you're not winning players over. Focus on making new heroes fun without being broken, and buff underpreforming ones. Ensure most heroes aren't completely opressed by a certain character and always have some counterplay, even if disadvantaged

TL;DR
Community is "ahh", but the game can be fun if you are into the team-based shooter genre and have friends to play with, but I would not recommend this to anybody.

Marvel Rivals is an incredible game, assuming the planets align, Mercury isn’t in retrograde, and matchmaking hasn’t chosen violence that day.

Queue times? Suspiciously fast. Like the game is luring you into a trap.
Updates? Constant. Blink and there’s a new patch, a new hero, and three new bugs with superpowers.
Gameplay? Chaotic, flashy, and so fast your frontal lobe has to overclock just to survive.

And then… the human element enters.

Every other match feels like you accidentally queued into the finals of an esports tournament while trying to test a character because “hey that raccoon looks fun.”
Smurfs are multiplying like they’re being farmed in a lab. I’ve gotten so many ban confirmations my inbox looks like I work internal affairs.
Bots? Oh they’re in there. Some move like confused Roombas. Others suddenly hit headshots like they were possessed by an angry deity.

Quick Match, by the way, is the biggest lie in modern gaming.

Wanna learn a new hero? Absolutely not.
Wanna relax after work? Cute.
Wanna play casually? Here’s six coordinated maniacs in matching skins moving as a single organism, all apparently communicating through military-grade comms.

You spawn in and immediately meet a Spider-Man who has 400 hours, no sunlight exposure, and personal beef with your bloodline.

And matchmaking? Bro.

You’re level 12, still figuring out what half your abilities do.

Your team:

A guy eating cereal mid-match
Someone named “healerpls” who instalocked DPS
A Moon Knight standing still, possibly astral projecting

Enemy team:

Four-stack sweat squad
One Jeff main who plays like he can see 8 seconds into the future
A Magneto moving objects and my self-esteem simultaneously

The skill gap is so dramatic it feels illegal. One side has “Timmy downloaded because Hulk looked cool.”

The other side has “XxVoidExecutionerxX,” whose family probably thinks he died years ago.

And somehow… somehow… I queue again.

10/10 Stockholm syndrome simulator.

This game looks and feels VERY familiar to Overwatch 2, but with different heroes and slightly different mechanics. Not an unique game compared to other related games that have their own style and feel.

The assets and map design used in Marvel Rivals are extremely simular to that of Overwatch 2. The only real major difference between these two games are the amount of playable characters, character abilities, custom team formats and buffs that certain characters receive when they are combined with other related characters in the same team.

From my experience Marvel Rivals is a copy pasted form of Overwatch 2 in terms of playstyle, feel, looks and enjoyment. If you like one, you'll probebly like the other.

Personally I think Marvel Rivals really lacks an unique selling point among simular games, which is a no-go for me.
